mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Imagine, for a moment, believing you'd finally gained your freedom... only to find new chains, hidden in plain sight. That's the unsettling reality we’ll explore together in the world revealed by Douglas A. Blackmon’s *Slavery by Another Name*. Even after the Emancipation Proclamation, a shadowy network of laws and practices kept countless Black Americans trapped in cycles of oppression—long past the Civil War and right up to World War II. What if liberty was just an illusion? Through stories of convict leasing, debt peonage, and forced labor—endorsed by legal systems and social institutions—we’ll uncover how freedom was twisted, and how entire communities were left to pick up the pieces. But this isn’t just a story of hardship—it’s about resilience, too. We’ll see how Black Americans found ways to resist and endure, even as families were torn apart and generations bore the scars of injustice. And as we journey through these pages, we’ll discover how the echoes of that era still shape our world today, challenging us to rethink what progress and justice really mean. So, let’s take this journey together—uncovering truths, honoring resilience, and seeking a deeper understanding of the forces that have shaped American history.
